subject: pilot whale
title: Orcas Run From One Animal, and It's Smaller Than They Are

scenes.text: Orcas hunt great whites. But off Iceland, they run from something smaller.
It's the long-finned pilot whale, actually a big dolphin.
In years of sightings, orcas moved away from pilot whales in about two out of three encounters.
In more than a quarter, they fled at high speed, leaping out of the water as they went.
In 2026, scientists played pilot whale calls to tagged orcas. The orcas bunched up, turned away and sped off.
Nobody knows why yet. The ocean's top predator has something it avoids.

description:
Off Iceland, killer whales moved away from long-finned pilot whales in 68% of observed encounters, and in 28% they fled at high speed.
In a 2026 Scientific Reports study, playback of pilot whale calls made tagged orcas group up, turn away and speed up. Why they avoid pilot whales is still unknown.
What do you think scares an orca?
first_comment: Competition, mobbing, or something else? What's your best guess for why orcas avoid them?
